record.what_it_does: All-in-one workspace for notes, docs, databases, wikis and project management.
record.auth_notes: Three credential types, all sent as Bearer in the Authorization header with a Notion-Version header. (1) Internal connection API token: static, scoped to one workspace. (2) Personal access token (PAT): created by a Notion user in the Developer portal, and acts with that user's permissions. (3) OAuth 2.0 for public connections, with token create, refresh, introspect and revoke endpoints. Users choose which pages to share. Multi-user toolkits should use a public OAuth connection.
record.access_notes: Free-plan workspaces can create connections, but on Free and Plus only workspace owners can do so. Business and Enterprise owners can let members create them. Public OAuth connections need no Marketplace submission or review; review applies only to a Marketplace listing. The pricing page lists "Public API" and "Webhooks" rows but showed no per-plan values. Business and Enterprise get higher rate limits. MCP bearer tokens are limited to Business and Enterprise, but that is separate from the REST API.
record.api_breadth_notes: Base URL https://api.notion.com, versioned with a Notion-Version header. llms.txt lists 77 endpoint reference pages, about 74 distinct operations. They cover tokens, blocks, pages (including markdown read/write), databases and data sources (plus legacy endpoints), views, comments, file uploads, search, users, custom emoji, meeting notes, Notion Agents and sessions, and agent skills. An OpenAPI 3.1 spec is published at developers.notion.com/openapi.json, alongside openapi-adminApi.json and openapi-undocumented.json.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.notion.com/mcp, hosted by Notion. It uses OAuth by default. MCP bearer tokens are available on Business and Enterprise only, and only workspace owners can create them. Business and Enterprise also get higher MCP rate limits.
record.blocker_notes: Public OAuth connections work without Marketplace review. On Free and Plus, only workspace owners can create the connection. End users must pick which pages the integration can access. There is no dedicated sandbox, but a free workspace can be used for testing.

evidence.quote: Marketplace submission or review is not required.
Personal access tokens (PATs) are created directly by a Notion user in the Developer portal.
On Free and Plus plans, only workspace owners can create connections.
Webhooks let your connection receive real-time updates from Notion.
